_note: L1 pt (Portuguese, Brazil): 37 extra clip rows for the reels pipeline.

in.wrong: She is teacher.
in.answer_say: The first! He is a doctor.

native.tip: Em inglês, antes de uma profissão usamos “a” ou “an”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She is teacher.” O certo é “She is a teacher.” Em português não precisamos do artigo, mas em inglês ele é obrigatório. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “He is a doctor.” Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, before a job we use “a” or “an”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She is teacher.” The right way is “She is a teacher.” Many learners drop the article, but English needs it. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Actually, I live in this city.
in.right: Currently, I live in this city.
in.answer_say: Currently!

native.tip: “Actually” quer dizer “na verdade”. “Atualmente” é “currently” ou “nowadays”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Actually, I live in this city.” O certo é “Currently, I live in this city.” Cuidado: é um falso cognato clássico. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “currently”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Actually” means “in fact”. For “these days”, use “currently” or “nowadays”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Actually, I live in this city.” The right way is “Currently, I live in this city.” Careful: it is a classic false friend. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I like very much pizza.
in.answer_say: The first! I like music very much.

native.tip: Em inglês, o objeto vem logo depois do verbo: “I like pizza very much”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I like very much pizza.” O certo é “I like pizza very much.” Em português dizemos “gosto muito de pizza”, mas a ordem em inglês é outra. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “I like music very much.” Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “like very much pizza”?
en.tip: In English, the object comes right after the verb: “I like pizza very much”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I like very much pizza.” The right way is “I like pizza very much.” Many learners copy the word order of their own language, but English puts the object first. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: It depends of the weather.
in.answer_say: On! It depends on you.

native.tip: O verbo “depend” é sempre seguido de “on”, nunca de “of”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “It depends of the weather.” O certo é “It depends on the weather.” Aqui o “de” do português atrapalha. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “on”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: The verb “depend” always goes with “on”, never “of”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “It depends of the weather.” The right way is “It depends on the weather.” Learners often carry over “de” from their own language, but English uses “on”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: We discuss about the plan.
in.answer_say: Discuss! We discuss the problem.

native.tip: “Discuss” já inclui o “sobre”. Não precisa de “about”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “We discuss about the plan.” O certo é “We discuss the plan.” É o famoso “discutir sobre” do português. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “discuss”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Discuss” already includes “about”. You do not need it.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “We discuss about the plan.” The right way is “We discuss the plan.” It comes from the common “discutir sobre” in the learner's own language. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I live here since 2020.
in.why: With since, use have and the past form.
in.answer_say: Have! I have worked here since May.

native.tip: Com “since” usamos o present perfect: “I have lived”, não “I live”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I live here since 2020.” O certo é “I have lived here since 2020.” Em português usamos o presente, mas o inglês pede outro tempo. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “have”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I live here since”?
en.tip: With “since” we use the present perfect: “I have lived”, not “I live”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I live here since 2020.” The right way is “I have lived here since 2020.” Many learners use the present here, but English needs the present perfect. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She gave me many informations.
in.right: She gave me a lot of information.
in.answer_say: Information! I need some information.

native.tip: “Information” não tem plural em inglês. Use “a lot of information”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She gave me many informations.” O certo é “She gave me a lot of information.” Em português é “informações”, mas o inglês não aceita o s. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “information”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Information” has no plural in English. Say “a lot of information”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She gave me many informations.” The right way is “She gave me a lot of information.” The plural “informações” feels natural, but English does not allow the s. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I bought a book at the library.
in.right: I bought a book at the bookstore.
in.why: A library lends books. It does not sell.

quiz.stem: I want to buy a book at the ___.

in.answer_say: Bookstore! I buy books at the bookstore.

native.tip: “Library” é biblioteca. Livraria é “bookstore”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I bought a book at the library.” O certo é “I bought a book at the bookstore.” Esse falso cognato confunde muita gente. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “bookstore”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Library” means a place to borrow books. A shop is a “bookstore”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I bought a book at the library.” The right way is “I bought a book at the bookstore.” This false friend confuses many learners. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am very exciting about the trip.
in.right: I am very excited about the trip.
in.why: I feel excited. A trip is exciting.
in.answer_say: Excited! I am excited about the party.

native.tip: Para sentimentos usamos “-ed”: “excited”. Para coisas, “-ing”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am very exciting about the trip.” O certo é “I am very excited about the trip.” Quem sente é “excited”; o que causa a emoção é “exciting”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “excited”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: For feelings we use “-ed”: “excited”. For things, “-ing”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am very exciting about the trip.” The right way is “I am very excited about the trip.” The person who feels is “excited”; the thing that causes it is “exciting”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My cousin is married with a doctor.
in.right: My cousin is married to a doctor.
in.answer_say: To! She is married to my brother.

native.tip: Em inglês, “casado com” é “married to”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “My cousin is married with a doctor.” O certo é “My cousin is married to a doctor.” O “com” do português não vira “with” aqui. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “to”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, “casado com” is “married to”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “My cousin is married with a doctor.” The right way is “My cousin is married to a doctor.” The usual “com” does not become “with” here. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am agree with you.
in.answer_say: Agree! I agree with you.

native.tip: “Agree” já é verbo. Não use “am” antes dele.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am agree with you.” O certo é “I agree with you.” Em português é “estou de acordo”, mas em inglês é só “agree”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “agree”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Agree” is already a verb. Do not put “am” before it.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am agree with you.” The right way is “I agree with you.” Learners think of “estou de acordo”, but in English it is just “agree”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: It has a lot of people here.
in.right: There are a lot of people here.
in.why: To say something exists, use there is or there are.
in.answer_say: There are! There are many people here.

native.tip: Para dizer que existe algo, use “there is” ou “there are”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “It has a lot of people here.” O certo é “There are a lot of people here.” O verbo “ter” do português tem dois usos; em inglês são dois verbos. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “There are”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: To say that something exists, use “there is” or “there are”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “It has a lot of people here.” The right way is “There are a lot of people here.” The verb “ter” has two uses; English uses two different verbs. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Is cold today.
in.answer_say: It! It is hot today.

native.tip: Em inglês, a frase precisa de sujeito: “It is cold”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Is cold today.” O certo é “It is cold today.” Em português dizemos “está frio”, sem sujeito. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “It”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, the sentence needs a subject: “It is cold”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Is cold today.” The right way is “It is cold today.” Learners say “está frio” with no subject, but English needs one. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to home after work.
in.answer_say: Go! I want to go home.

native.tip: Com “home”, não usamos “to”: “go home”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I go to home after work.” O certo é “I go home after work.” Home é uma exceção que vale decorar. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “go”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “home”, we do not use “to”: “go home”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I go to home after work.” The right way is “I go home after work.” Home is an exception worth remembering. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She don't like coffee.
in.answer_say: Doesn't! He doesn't like tea.

native.tip: Com “he”, “she” e “it” usamos “doesn't”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She don't like coffee.” O certo é “She doesn't like coffee.” Em português o verbo muda na terminação, mas em inglês “she” pede “doesn't”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “doesn't”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “he”, “she” and “it” we use “doesn't”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She don't like coffee.” The right way is “She doesn't like coffee.” In their own language the verb ending changes, but in English “she” needs “doesn't”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I need to make my homework.
in.right: I need to do my homework.
in.answer_say: Do! I always do my homework.

native.tip: Tarefa de casa é “do homework”. Em português usamos “fazer” para tudo.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I need to make my homework.” O certo é “I need to do my homework.” Em inglês, “fazer” se divide em “make” e “do”. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “do”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: Homework goes with “do”: “do homework”. “Fazer” is one word, but English splits it into “make” and “do”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I need to make my homework.” The right way is “I need to do my homework.” In English, “fazer” splits into “make” and “do”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
in.right: I will call you when I arrive.
in.answer_say: Arrive! Call me when you arrive.

native.tip: Depois de “when”, usamos o presente, não o futuro.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I will call you when I will arrive.” O certo é “I will call you when I arrive.” Em português usamos o futuro do subjuntivo (“quando eu chegar”), mas em inglês vem o presente. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “arrive”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “when I will arrive”?
en.tip: After “when”, we use the present, not the future.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I will call you when I will arrive.” The right way is “I will call you when I arrive.” Learners use a future form (“quando eu chegar”), but English uses the present. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Where you live?
in.answer_say: Do! Where do you work?

native.tip: Nas perguntas, precisamos do auxiliar “do” ou “does”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Where you live?” O certo é “Where do you live?” Em português basta mudar a entonação; em inglês não. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “do”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In questions, we need the helper “do” or “does”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Where you live?” The right way is “Where do you live?” Learners think the tone is enough, but English needs “do”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I want that you help me.
in.right: I want you to help me.
in.answer_say: To! I want you to come.

native.tip: Em inglês dizemos “want you to”, sem “that”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I want that you help me.” O certo é “I want you to help me.” Em português usamos “quero que você”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “to”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I want that you”?
en.tip: In English we say “want you to”, with no “that”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I want that you help me.” The right way is “I want you to help me.” Learners copy “quero que você”, but English says “want you to”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Can you borrow me a pen?
in.right: Can you lend me a pen?
in.answer_say: Lend! Can you lend me your phone?

native.tip: Quem empresta é “lend”. Quem pede emprestado é “borrow”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Can you borrow me a pen?” O certo é “Can you lend me a pen?” Em português usamos “emprestar” para os dois lados. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “lend”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: The giver “lends”. The one who asks “borrows”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Can you borrow me a pen?” The right way is “Can you lend me a pen?” The word “emprestar” works both ways, but English uses two verbs. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: He said me the truth.
in.answer_say: Told! She told me a secret.

native.tip: Com a pessoa logo depois do verbo, use “tell”: “told me”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “He said me the truth.” O certo é “He told me the truth.” “Me disse” vira “told me”, não “said me”. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “told”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: When a person comes right after the verb, use “tell”: “told me”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “He said me the truth.” The right way is “He told me the truth.” “Me disse” becomes “told me”, not “said me”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I have a doubt about this word.
in.right: I have a question about this word.
in.why: Doubt means you are not sure.

quiz.stem: I have a ___ about the test.

in.answer_say: Question! I have a question about the test.

native.tip: “Doubt” é incerteza, não ter certeza. Para perguntar algo, diga “I have a question”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I have a doubt about this word.” O certo é “I have a question about this word.” Na sala de aula, esse erro aparece o tempo todo. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “question”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Doubt” means you are not sure. To ask something, say “I have a question”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I have a doubt about this word.” The right way is “I have a question about this word.” This mistake shows up in class all the time. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She speaks more better than me.
in.answer_say: Better! This is better than that.

native.tip: “Better” já é comparativo. Não precisa de “more”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She speaks more better than me.” O certo é “She speaks better than me.” É como dizer “mais melhor” em português. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “better”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Better” is already a comparative. You do not need “more”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She speaks more better than me.” The right way is “She speaks better than me.” It is like saying “mais melhor” in the learner's own language. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I lost the bus this morning.
in.right: I missed the bus this morning.

quiz.stem: Hurry or you will ___ the train.

in.answer_say: Miss! You will miss the train.

native.tip: Quando “perde” o ônibus, use “miss”. “Lose” é para objetos.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I lost the bus this morning.” O certo é “I missed the bus this morning.” Em português “perder” serve para os dois casos. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “miss”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I lost the bus”?
en.tip: For a bus or a train, use “miss”. “Lose” is for objects.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I lost the bus this morning.” The right way is “I missed the bus this morning.” The word “perder” covers both cases, but English uses two verbs. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I have been in Paris last year.
in.right: I was in Paris last year.
in.answer_say: Was! I was at home last week.

native.tip: Com “last year” (tempo passado definido), use o passado simples.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I have been in Paris last year.” O certo é “I was in Paris last year.” Muita gente traduz “estive” como “have been”, mas com “last year” o inglês pede o passado simples. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “was”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “have been last year”?
en.tip: With “last year” (a finished time), use the simple past.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I have been in Paris last year.” The right way is “I was in Paris last year.” Many learners translate “estive” as “have been”, but with “last year” English needs the simple past. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: On the bus, not in the bus!
in.wrong: I am in the bus now.
in.right: I am on the bus now.
in.memory: On the bus, in the car.
in.answer_say: On! I am on the train.

native.tip: Para ônibus, trem e avião, usamos “on.” Para carro, “in.”
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am in the bus now.” O certo é “I am on the bus now.” Em português dizemos “no ônibus”, mas o inglês separa “on” e “in.” Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “on”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: For buses, trains, and planes, we use “on.” For cars, “in.”
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am in the bus now.” The right way is “I am on the bus now.” In your language, it is “no ônibus”, but English splits “on” and “in.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My hair are brown.
in.answer_say: Is! Her hair is long.

native.tip: “Hair” é incontável em inglês: “my hair is”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “My hair are brown.” O certo é “My hair is brown.” Às vezes dizemos “cabelos”, mas “hair” é incontável e pede “is”. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “is”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Hair” is uncountable in English: “my hair is”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “My hair are brown.” The right way is “My hair is brown.” Learners sometimes say “cabelos”, but “hair” is uncountable and takes “is”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.hook_say: Two no words? Not in English!
in.wrong: I do not know nothing.
in.answer_say: Any! I do not have any money.

native.tip: Em português “não sei nada” tem dois negativos; em inglês, com “do not”, use “anything”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I do not know nothing.” O certo é “I do not know anything.” Em português a dupla negação é normal, mas em inglês um negativo basta. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “any”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: Double negatives feel normal to many learners. In English, with “do not”, use “anything”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I do not know nothing.” The right way is “I do not know anything.” A double negative feels normal to many learners, but in English one negative is enough. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I assisted a movie last night.
in.right: I watched a movie last night.
in.answer_say: Watched! I watched a movie last night.

native.tip: Em português “assistir” um filme é ver; em inglês “assist” é ajudar. Para filme, use “watch”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I assisted a movie last night.” O certo é “I watched a movie last night.” É um falso cognato: o “assistir” português vira “watch” em inglês. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “watched”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Assistir” a movie means to watch it, but “assist” means to help. For a movie, use “watch”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I assisted a movie last night.” The right way is “I watched a movie last night.” It is a false friend: “assistir” becomes “watch” in English. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I passed two days at home.
in.right: I spent two days at home.

quiz.stem: I ___ two hours on this video.

in.answer_say: Spent! I spent two hours on it.

native.tip: Em português dizemos “passei dois dias em casa”; em inglês, para tempo, o natural é “spend”: “I spent”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I passed two days at home.” O certo é “I spent two days at home.” Aqui o “passar” não funciona: em inglês o tempo é gasto, “spend”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
